title: Incorporate chaos-derived failure modes and deterministic acceptance tests into Serving PRD
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: After the recent chaos run and follow-up postmortem, several intermittent failure modes were identified that are not currently encoded in the Serving PRD acceptance criteria. This ticket updates the PRD to include: explicit failure-mode descriptions, deterministic acceptance tests derived from chaos scenarios, canary gating rules, rollback thresholds, and observable telemetry events required for automated release decisions.
background: A chaos experiment run in staging (2026-02) surfaced three reproducible classes of failures: (1) KV cache bake/corruption during rapid autoscale events leading to 95th/99th latency spikes, (2) degraded batching behavior when node churn coincides with large prefix-cache hits, and (3) sporadic kernel fallback that produced silent output mismatches. The postmortem recommended codifying these into the PRD so product, eng, and QE have a shared, testable contract before rollout.
problem_statement: Current PRD acceptance criteria are high-level (e.g., "no regression vs baseline"). Without scenario-specific tests and release gates, regressions discovered only in production cause customer impact and longer rollback windows. We need explicit, reproducible tests and guardrails to prevent shipping regressions tied to chaos-derived failure modes.
proposal: Expand the Serving PRD to include: 1) enumerated failure mode descriptions with severity, 2) deterministic synthetic tests that reproduce each failure mode in CI/staging, 3) canary progression and automated rollback thresholds derived from target SLO deltas, 4) telemetry events and dashboards required for go/no-go, and 5) an acceptance checklist for QE and product sign-off. The PRD will require engineering to deliver test harnesses and observability metrics as part of any kernel/runtime change.
scope: In scope: updating the Serving PRD document text, adding acceptance-test definitions, listing required telemetry and dashboard panels, defining canary progression rules for dedicated and hosted tiers, and enumerating automated rollback thresholds. Implementation tasks (test harness, dashboards, canary rollout automation) should be tracked in separate ENG tickets but linked here.
out_of_scope: Full implementation of all automated rollbacks (ENG tickets will own this), on-prem installation packaging, and customer-facing doc updates (will be handled after PRD acceptance).
acceptance_criteria: PRD updated with a 'Chaos-derived failure modes' section that lists at least three failure modes, severity, and reproducible steps.
For each failure mode, there is a deterministic acceptance test (script or harness) documented with inputs, expected outputs, and run instructions that QE can execute in CI/staging.
Canary progression rules added: explicit metric thresholds for progressing from 10% -> 50% -> 100% traffic, and automated rollback triggers defined (example thresholds included).

Required telemetry events and dashboard panels enumerated (latency percentiles, per-model KV cache hit/miss, kernel-fallback-rate, batch size distribution), with links to expected dashboards or mockups.
SLO/regression criteria codified: changes that increase 95th latency by >25ms or increase kernel-fallback-rate above 0.5% for 15 minutes must block rollout.
Product and QE sign-off checklist appended to PRD and signed by assignee and QE lead before release to canary.
A set of initial ENG stories created and linked that implement the acceptance tests and dashboards.
Updated PRD includes a 'rollback runbook' section with playbook steps, owners, and verification steps for post-rollback validation.
success_metrics: Canary detect-and-rollback rate for chaos-derived failure modes is >90% in staging during the verification window
Time-to-detect for injected KV cache corruption in staging < 2 minutes using the new telemetry
Reduction in production incidents related to KV-cache/autoscale by 75% in the quarter after release
No customer-facing regression attributable to kernel-fallback changes in the first 4 weeks of a release
rollout_plan: Update PRD and circulate for 1-week review with ENG, QE, Design, and Security
Create ENG stories for test harness, dashboards, and canary automation (target two-week sprint for stubbed telemetry)
Run acceptance tests in staging against a canary build while running chaos injection; verify canary progression rules and rollback behavior
Perform cross-functional sign-off (Product, ENG, QE) and schedule release to limited-hosted region with 10% traffic
Monitor canary for 72 hours, progress to 50% if thresholds met, then 100% after 7 days without violations
Post-release: 30-day incident watch and scheduled retro to validate acceptance criteria effectiveness
test_plan: Deterministic KV-corruption harness: script to flip specific KV entries and assert detection via checksum/telemetry
Autoscale churn scenario: scripted node add/remove while generating high prefix-cache hit traffic to verify batching and latency SLOs
Kernel-fallback synthetic mismatch test: feed canonical prompts and compare outputs across fallback and primary kernels to assert no silent changes
Nightly chaos sweep in staging that runs the three scenarios with alerting to the on-call and QE dashboard
CI job that runs the deterministic tests on PRs touching runtime or kernel selection code

ENG: Create test harness tickets and implement KV-corruption script (ENG-7821)
QE: Integrate deterministic tests into CI and staging jobs (QE-129)

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Deterministic tests produce flakiness and block PRs. Mitigation: run heavy/chaos tests only on nightly or gated canary builds; keep CI fast by splitting test tiers.
Risk: Overly strict rollback thresholds prevent shipping important performance improvements. Mitigation: include 'grace window' and escalation path in PRD for controlled exceptions.
Risk: Engineering capacity to implement test harness is limited. Mitigation: prioritize minimal reproducible harness (PoC) and iterate; track full implementation as follow-up ENG work.
Risk: Missing telemetry coverage. Mitigation: require telemetry events as part of PR acceptance criteria for any runtime change.

Risk: Customer-specific edge cases not covered by the three scenarios. Mitigation: add field reports and customer repros to the 'continuous learning' section of the PRD and schedule quarterly chaos reviews.
open_questions: Who will be the long-term owner for maintaining the deterministic test harness? (suggest ENG-QE collaboration)
Should canary thresholds differ between hosted API and Dedicated capacity customers? (proposal: more conservative for dedicated customers)
What SLO delta constitutes an 'acceptable regression' for experimental features vs bugfixes?
Are there cost limits for running nightly chaos tests in staging? Should we cap test duration?
